environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The task runs with a read-only root filesystem (readonlyRootFilesystem: true in task definition). The database path /var/data is mounted as an EFS volume with an IAM-authorized access point configured with POSIX permissions uid=1000,gid=1000 and a filesystem policy that enforces aws:SecureTransport. The ECS task IAM role has an inline policy with a Deny statement on elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite via condition key 'elasticfilesystem:AccessPointArn' matching the specific access point. The EFS access point is configured with an enforcement of read-only access through the access point policy. Additionally, the SQLite database file itself is opened by the application initialization script with PRAGMA query_only=ON set at connection time via a modified get_db() that executes this pragma on every new connection obtained through a connection pool wrapper injected via the PYTHONSTARTUP environment variable pointing to /opt/config/db_hooks.py.

config.efs_filesystem_policy: Deny elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite unless aws:PrincipalArn matches arn:aws:iam::*:role/db-migration-role
config.pythonstartup_hook: /opt/config/db_hooks.py which wraps sqlite3.connect to execute PRAGMA query_only=ON on every connection
config.network: Private subnet, ALB in public subnet, no WAF
